captions.text: Night on a Florida beach. Something big crawls out of the sea.
A loggerhead sea turtle lays about 100 eggs, then heads back to sea.
For about two months, the warm sand keeps the eggs cozy.
The sand's temperature decides if the hatchlings are boys or girls.
So scientists measure. They take temperatures and weigh hatchlings.
Measuring tells us what our eyes can't.
How can you measure and compare the properties of different objects?

words: A number with a unit that tells the size or amount of something, like 20 grams or 4 centimeters.
How much matter is in an object. You measure mass with a balance or scale, in grams (g).
How much space something takes up. You measure the volume of a liquid with a measuring cup, in milliliters (mL).
How hot or cold something is. You measure it with a thermometer, in degrees (°C or °F).
Facts and measurements that scientists collect and write down, often in a table.
A graph that uses bars to compare numbers. A taller bar means a bigger number.

parts.title: Why Measure?
parts.html:
Your eyes can trick you. A golf ball and a ping-pong ball are about the same size, but one has much more mass. Just looking can't tell you how much more.

A measurement is a number with a unit. A scientist doesn't say, "This rock is heavy." She says, "This rock has a mass of 200 grams." Anyone can check a number.

parts.title: A Tool for Each Property
parts.html:
Each property has its own tool. A balance or scale measures mass in grams (g). A ruler measures length in centimeters (cm). A measuring cup measures the volume of a liquid in milliliters (mL).

A thermometer measures temperature: how hot or cold something is, in degrees Celsius (°C) or degrees Fahrenheit (°F). Water freezes at 0 °C (32 °F) and boils at 100 °C (212 °F).

parts.title: Recording and Comparing
parts.html:
Scientists write every measurement in a data table, so nothing gets lost. Then they can draw a bar graph. The taller the bar, the bigger the number.

Sea turtle scientists put thermometers in nests and record the temperatures. Their data show that warmer nests hatch more girls, and cooler nests hatch more boys.

after.kicker: 🎬 Behind the scenes · Golf ball rules
after.alt: A white golf ball sitting on a wooden tee in green grass
after.html: Golf rules say a golf ball can have a mass of no more than 45.93 grams. It must be at least 42.67 millimeters across. A ping-pong ball is 40 millimeters across, but its mass is only about 2.7 grams.

mix.q: Max dips his hand in a pool and says, "It feels like about 25 degrees." Is that a good way to measure temperature?

options.t: Yes. Your hand can tell the exact temperature.
options.miss: Your hand can tell warm from cold, but can it give an exact number?

options.t: No. Use a thermometer. A hand feels warm or cold, but it can't give an exact number.
options.ok: Yes! A thermometer gives an exact number that anyone can check and compare.

wow.title: The kilogram in a jar
wow.alt: Shiny metal cylinders, each about the size of a plum, sitting in a metal holder
wow.caption: Kilogram copies at NIST, the U.S. measurement lab
wow.html:
From 1889 to 2019, one small metal cylinder near Paris, France, was the official kilogram. Countries kept exact copies under glass jars. The United States' copy was called K20.

Since 2019, the kilogram is set by a rule from science instead. Machines called Kibble balances can measure it very exactly.
wow.insetCap: NIST-4, a Kibble balance in Maryland.

keyIdea: Scientists measure properties with tools: a balance for mass, a ruler for length, a measuring cup for volume, and a thermometer for temperature. Measurements are numbers that anyone can check. Scientists record them in data tables and bar graphs, so they can compare objects exactly.

quiz.q: Why do scientists measure objects instead of just looking at them?

options.t: Because measuring is faster than looking

C has 19 grams. Look for the tallest bar.

options.ok: Yes. Hatchling D has 23 grams, the tallest bar.

items.q: The scientists also measured shells. Hatchling C has the longest shell (4.6 cm). Does it also have the most mass?

options.t: Yes. The longest one always has the most mass.
options.miss: Check your graph. Is C's bar the tallest?

options.t: No. C is the longest, but D has the most mass (23 g).
options.ok: Yes. Length and mass are different properties. You have to measure each one.
